# `canair search`

```
usage: canair search [-h] <kind> ...

[UDS] Find a string, VIN or byte pattern anywhere in the captures — without already
knowing which ECU and PID holds it.

Choose a domain kind:
  uds   diagnostic captures (default) — payload bytes, labels, notes
        (domain A). A bare `canair search …` is shorthand for this.

With a PATTERN it finds that needle; with none it inventories every
plausible string (part numbers, versions, ECU names). Read-only: searches
captures/ only, never talks to the device.

positional arguments:
  <kind>
    uds       Search diagnostic capture payloads, labels and notes (domain A)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

examples:
  # which ECU/PID holds this part number (or any substring of it)?
  canair search 95400G7470

  # list every plausible string in the captures: part numbers, versions, ECU names
  canair search

  # a regular expression, case-sensitive
  canair search --regex 'G[0-9]{4}' --case-sensitive

  # anything VIN-shaped, in payloads and in labels/notes
  canair search --vin

  # a byte pattern, wherever it occurs in any payload
  canair search --hex 'DE AD BE EF' --query BMS

  # include the decoded identity fields in ecus/, and emit machine-readable output
  canair search KMHC --defs --json

Each payload hit carries a paste-ready `pids upsert-param ... --type ascii` command, so
a string you found can be defined as a signal in one step.
```

## `canair search uds`

```
usage: canair search uds [-h] [--regex] [--hex BYTES] [--vin]
                         [--case-sensitive] [--in {payload,text,all}] [--defs]
                         [--query QUERY] [--min-len N] [--all-runs]
                         [--limit N] [--json] [--notation NAME] [--since WHEN]
                         [--until WHEN] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--today]
                         [--last-sessions [N]] [--last-session]
                         [--state STATE] [--label SUBSTR]
                         [PATTERN]

Search every captured payload (and, by default, labels and notes) for a string, VIN or byte pattern; or, with no PATTERN, list every plausible string. Findings are grouped by location (ECU, PID, offset), not by capture, with a hit count and first/last-seen date.

positional arguments:
  PATTERN               Literal substring, case-insensitive (omit to list
                        every plausible string)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --notation NAME       byte-index notation for output labels: wican
                        (default), isotp, torque, bix. Overrides the
                        display.byte_notation config key.

match:
  --regex               Treat PATTERN as a regular expression
  --hex BYTES           Search payloads for a byte pattern instead of text
                        (e.g. 'DE AD BE EF')
  --vin                 Shortcut for anything VIN-shaped (17 characters, ISO
                        3779, at least one letter)
  --case-sensitive      Make a text PATTERN honour case

haystack:
  --in {payload,text,all}
                        Where to look: payload bytes, free text (labels,
                        notes, text responses), or all (default). Note that
                        --label NARROWS to matching sessions, whereas a
                        PATTERN searches (labels included, by default)
  --defs                Also search the ecus/ identity fields (part numbers,
                        serials, versions)
  --query QUERY         Narrow to ECU/PID selectors in the shared mini-
                        language (e.g. 'BMS', 'BCM:22F188', 'VCU BMS')

inventory (no PATTERN):
  --min-len N           Minimum printable run length (default 6)
  --all-runs            Disable the plausibility filter (raw strings(1)
                        behaviour — mostly noise: numeric telemetry bytes are
                        often printable)

output:
  --limit N             Show at most N findings (default 50; 0 = no cap). A
                        footer reports any hidden
  --json                Machine-readable output

scoping:
  Restrict to captures within a date/time range (inclusive) and/or by session state (token-matched) or label substring. --since/--until accept a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS[.ffffff]])

  --since WHEN          Only captures on or after this date/time (YYYY-MM-DD[
                        HH:MM:SS])
  --until WHEN          Only captures on or before this date/time (YYYY-MM-DD[
                        HH:MM:SS])
  --date YYYY-MM-DD     Only captures on this exact date (shorthand for
                        --since X --until X)
  --today               Only captures recorded today (shorthand for --date
                        <today>)
  --last-sessions [N]   Only the most recent N recorded sessions in scope (N
                        defaults to 1)
  --last-session        Only the most recent recorded session in scope (alias
                        for --last-sessions 1)
  --state STATE         Only captures recorded in STATE, matched by token and
                        widened by the profile's implies: hierarchy (--state
                        ready also matches DRIVING). Comma-separate
                        alternatives (--state ready,driving); repeat the flag
                        to require several at once (--state charging --state
                        parked)
  --label SUBSTR        Only captures whose session/capture label contains
                        SUBSTR (case-insensitive)

examples:
  # which ECU/PID holds this part number (or any substring of it)?
  canair search 95400G7470

  # list every plausible string in the captures: part numbers, versions, ECU names
  canair search

  # a regular expression, case-sensitive
  canair search --regex 'G[0-9]{4}' --case-sensitive

  # anything VIN-shaped, in payloads and in labels/notes
  canair search --vin

  # a byte pattern, wherever it occurs in any payload
  canair search --hex 'DE AD BE EF' --query BMS

  # include the decoded identity fields in ecus/, and emit machine-readable output
  canair search KMHC --defs --json

Each payload hit carries a paste-ready `pids upsert-param ... --type ascii` command, so
a string you found can be defined as a signal in one step.
```
